w: Founded, so the temple claims, in 1376 - though the date is disputed - this is one of the few Buddhist temples in Korea built directly on the coast. Paper lanterns blanket the complex for Buddha's Birthday, and the shrine honors Haesu Gwaneum, the Sea Goddess Buddha of Mercy, watching the waves below.
s: Seaside temple with a legendary sea goddess
_facts: Claims founding in 1376, disputed
One of few Korean temples built on the seaside
Honors Haesu Gwaneum, Sea Goddess Buddha of Mercy
Decorated with paper lanterns for Buddha's Birthday

w: Named for the gravel (jagal) that once covered its shore, this is reckoned Korea's largest fish market, its stalls run since the postwar years by the fabled 'Jagalchi Ajumma' - women who sold catch on the street after the Korean War. Every autumn the waterfront turns over to a festival: 'Come! See! Buy!'
s: Korea's biggest fish market, named for gravel
_facts: Name derives from 'jagal' meaning gravel
Considered Korea's largest fish market
Known for female vendors called Jagalchi Ajumma, a postwar tradition
Hosts the Busan Jagalchi Festival each autumn

w: Once a true island off the west end of Haeundae Beach, its name means 'camellia island' for the trees that still cover its wooded headland. Designated a monument of Busan in 1999, it's now a peninsula whose coastal path threads pine groves and sea cliffs before circling back to the sand.
s: A camellia island turned scenic sea path
_facts: Formerly an island, now a peninsula at west end of Haeundae Beach
Name means 'camellia island'
Designated a Busan monument on March 9, 1999

w: Seven tumuli complexes scattered across South Korea tell the story of the Gaya confederacy, a federation of city-states that thrived from the 1st to the late 6th century before fading from history. In 2023 UNESCO inscribed the complexes as a World Heritage Site, cementing Gaya's place beside its better-known neighbors.
s: UNESCO burial mounds of a lost kingdom
_facts: Seven tumuli complexes of the Gaya confederacy
Span 1st to late 6th century CE
Listed as UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2023

w: Founded in 1945 in an empty lot selling goods left by departing Japanese colonists, this market changed names twice - Dotegi, then Jayu, then finally Gukje ('international') - as it grew through the Korean War refugee influx. Today it spans six zones and twelve buildings, immortalized in the film Ode to My Father.
s: A refugee market that outgrew its name twice
_facts: Founded 1945, originally Dotegi Market
Renamed Jayu (free) Market, then Gukje (international) Market
Became a commerce hub during the 1950-53 Korean War
Depicted in the 2014 film Ode to My Father

w: Whether you count five islands or six depends on the tide - the one closest to shore splits in two at high water, how these volcanic islets got their name, 'Five-Six Island.' Formed 80 million years ago and mapped since 1740, they're now viewed from the Oryukdo Skywalk, a glass platform over the cliff.
s: Five islands, or six, depending on the tide
_facts: Name reflects that the group appears as five or six islands depending on tide
Formed by volcanic activity 80 million years ago
Described in the 1740 text Tongnaebuji
Oryukdo Skywalk glass platform opened 2013

w: First raised in 1605 to honor Song Sanghyeon, who died defending Dongnae against the 1592 Japanese invasion, this shrine was renamed, relocated, and expanded across two centuries as more of the fallen were gathered into its halls, where rites are still performed today.
s: A shrine rebuilt for Busan's war dead of 1592
_facts: First built 1605 as Songgongsa to honor Song Sanghyeon
Renamed Chungnyeolsa in 1624
Relocated to current site in 1625
By 1736 all commemorated fighters gathered into one shrine

w: Completed in 1934 as a bascule bridge, its span once lifted daily to let ships through the harbor. During the Korean War, families scattered by the fighting gathered beneath it hoping to find each other. The lifting mechanism failed in 1966, and it was nearly demolished before restoration reopened it in 2013.
s: The bridge where Korean War families reunited
_facts: Completed 1934, a bascule (drawbridge)
Served as a site where Korean War refugees sought lost family
Drawbridge function stopped in 1966
Restored and reopened November 27, 2013

w: This modest building served as the residence of President Syngman Rhee during the Korean War, when Busan stood in as South Korea's provisional capital while Seoul lay in enemy hands. It's now a museum preserving that improvised wartime government - a whole capital squeezed into a borrowed house.
s: Where Korea's leader worked during the war
_facts: Used by President Syngman Rhee when Busan was provisional capital
Now a museum in Seo District

w: Built in 1593 by the Japanese general Kuroda Nagamasa to hold ground against the Joseon army during the Imjin War, this stone fortress once stood three storeys and about 300 metres around, its stones recycled from an older fort nearby. It sits quietly among farm fields today.
s: A 1593 Japanese fortress dug into the coast
_facts: Built 1593 by general Kuroda Nagamasa during the Imjin War
About 300 metres in circumference, three storeys, 4 metres high
Built from stones of the older Dumopojinseong fortress
Linked strategically to Ulsan and Busanjinseong fortresses

w: South Korea's third-largest museum holds more than 12,000 maritime relics, headlined by a replica of a Joseon-era mission ship built at half true size. Opened in 2012 on Yeongdo's waterfront, it rounds out its halls with a 4D theatre and small aquariums - a deep dive into a seafaring nation's history.
s: 12,000 relics and a half-scale Joseon ship
_facts: Third largest museum in South Korea
Opened July 9, 2012 in Yeongdo-gu
Exhibits more than 12,000 maritime relics including a half-size Joseon Missional Ship replica
Includes a 4D theatre and aquariums

w: A 634-metre mountain rising directly behind Haeundae District, its slopes give hikers a clear climb from city sprawl to a summit view over Busan's most famous beach - modest in height but hard to miss on the skyline behind the sand.
s: A 634m peak rising over Haeundae Beach
_facts: Mountain in Haeundae District
Elevation 634 metres
